title: Revenue Per Category
flavorText: SUM inside a GROUP BY aggregates independently per group — giving you a subtotal for each bucket.
narrative: Calculate the total stock value per category to see which is the most capital-intensive.
schemaSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL, stock INTEGER NOT NULL);
seedSql: INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Datapad','Electronics',299.99,45),(2,'Power Cell','Electronics',19.99,200),(3,'Steel Cable','Hardware',8.50,500),(4,'Logic Board','Electronics',89.99,30),(5,'Ceramic Fuse','Hardware',2.25,1000),(6,'Optic Lens','Optics',149.99,15),(7,'Servo Motor','Robotics',55.00,80),(8,'Pressure Valve','Hardware',12.75,300);
task: For each category, calculate the total stock value (price × stock). Order by total_value descending.

hints.text: Combine SUM(price * stock) with GROUP BY category to get a subtotal per category.
SELECT category, SUM(price * stock) AS total_value FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY total_value DESC;
SELECT category, SUM(price * stock) AS total_value FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY total_value DESC;
